meta.name: US Staffing Payroll Compliance Dataset
meta.disclaimer: Reference information compiled from official government sources. Not legal or tax advice. Check the cited source before relying on any value.

facts.value: next regular payday or within 15 days of discharge, whichever occurs first
facts.summary: Louisiana: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due next regular payday or within 15 days of discharge, whichever occurs first.
facts.evidence_quote: A.(1)(a) Upon the discharge of any laborer or other employee ... on or before the next regular payday or no later than fifteen days following the date of discharge, whichever occurs first.
facts.source_title: Louisiana R.S. 23:631, Discharge or resignation of employees

facts.value: next regular payday for that pay cycle or within 15 days of resignation, whichever occurs first
facts.summary: Louisiana: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due next regular payday for that pay cycle or within 15 days of resignation, whichever occurs first.
facts.evidence_quote: (b) Upon the resignation of any laborer or other employee ... on or before the next regular payday for the pay cycle during which the employee was working at the time of separation or no later than fifteen days following the date of resignation, whichever occurs first.
facts.source_title: Louisiana R.S. 23:631, Discharge or resignation of employees

facts.value: No state minimum wage law (federal $7.25 applies to FLSA-covered employers)
facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Louisiana basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: No state minimum wage law (federal $7.25 applies to FLSA-covered employers).
facts.evidence_quote: No state minimum wage law. Employers subject to the Fair Labor Standards Act must pay the current Federal minimum wage of $7.25 per hour.
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.summary: Louisiana independent contractor reporting required? (per OCSE): No
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.summary: Louisiana new hire reporting timeframe (per OCSE): Within 20 days of hire date
facts.evidence_quote: Reporting Timeframe: Within 20 days of hire date
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Federal floor is 20 days; states may set shorter deadlines. Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.summary: Louisiana: frequencies marked in the U.S. DOL State Payday Requirements table: Bi-weekly; Semi-monthly (note 7).
facts.source_title: State Payday Requirements (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Note 7: Louisiana. Applicable to entities employing 10 or more employees that are engaged in manufacturing, mining, or boring for oil, and to every public service corporation. Payment is required no less than twice during each calendar month. | DOL table last revised 2023-01-01; DOL says to consult the state labor office for official information. Confirm against current state law before relying on it.

facts.summary: Louisiana is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration

facts.summary: Louisiana base new employer UI rate: Industry average (IndAvg).
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance
facts.notes: DOL footnote 3: min/max rates apply only to experience-rated employers and exclude surtaxes, surcharges and non-UI taxes. Footnote 4: new employer rate shown is the base rate; higher rates may apply by industry or other factors. DOL notes the report is not an official interpretation of state law. IndAvg means the new employer rate is the industry average rate; get the exact rate from the state agency. Rate basis: DOL base rate. It may exclude mandatory surcharges, fund-building rates and assessments; check the state agency or total_new_employer_rate where available.

facts.summary: Louisiana experience-rated UI tax rates range from 0.09% to 6.00%.
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance
facts.notes: DOL footnote 3: min/max rates apply only to experience-rated employers and exclude surtaxes, surcharges and non-UI taxes. Footnote 4: new employer rate shown is the base rate; higher rates may apply by industry or other factors. DOL notes the report is not an official interpretation of state law.

facts.summary: Louisiana state unemployment taxable wage base: $7,000 per employee.
